acceptanceCriteria: Fixture corpus with 10,000 pinned inputs: build, `docs corpus query`, and each `corvint-corpus-mcp` tool succeed; the reported Git operation count per read is <= a small constant (e.g. <= 16) independent of input count.
Fixture with 2,000 non-indexed text inputs (html/erb/json) in one scope: `docs corpus manifest` and `docs corpus build` succeed.
A corpus that exceeds a documented capacity limit fails in < 1 s with a typed capacity code naming the limit (never `internal-error`).
Freshness still reports `stale` when one of the 10,000 inputs changes (regression guard for the batched path).
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1240 (filed 2026-10-19 against build main-fa8afe6). Every documentation-corpus read revalidates each pinned input with one Git tree lookup, charged against a fixed 1,024-operation budget (`gitrun.NewDefaultBudget`). A corpus with more than ~1,024 pinned inputs therefore cannot be read at all: every CLI query and every `corvint-corpus-mcp` tool call fails with `git-budget-exceeded`, after a long rebuild. The same per-input charging applies at build and at `docs corpus manifest`: every input the source index does not load as text (for example `.html`, `.erb`, `.scss`, `.json`, `.csv`, `.rake`, `.properties`, template files) costs one tree lookup plus one blob read, so a scope with several hundred such files exceeds the budget at build time.  The budget is a per-verification constant, not scaled to the manifest, and the result is surfaced as `internal-error` rather than a typed capacity refusal.
title: Corpus reads and builds fail with git-budget-exceeded past ~1,024 pinned inputs; batch freshness/blob reads and type capacity refusals (GitHub #1240)
